title: Isomorphisms from the direct-image fibre on both opens
statement: With the normalized restriction and right-adjoint data of [lem-sp-ringed-topos-direct-image-restriction], let A,B have an overlap isomorphism c. In any distinguished triangle G→RU A⊕RV B→RW(B|W)→G[1] whose middle map is the canonical adjunction-mate difference, the U-restriction of the first arrow followed by first projection and counit is invertible; the V-restriction followed by second projection and counit is invertible. A cover and left adjoints are not required.

source.place: Tag 08DG, right-direct-image and fibre calculation, extended to subterminal slices.

proof.text: Lift qU,qV through localization to identify the restrictions with the exact triangulated functors, transporting their shift structures and triangulatedness.

In a distinguished triangle G→X⊕Y→Z→G[1] with middle map (a,b) and b invertible, the middle map is split epic, the connecting map is zero, and the first map f is monic. Using f(a,b)=0 shows the X-projection is monic. The graph map (1,-ab^{-1}) is killed by (a,b), so coyoneda exactness factors it through f, yielding a section of the X-projection. It is therefore invertible. Swap summands for the Y-projection version.

Apply this argument to each restricted triangle. The cross-restriction lemma makes the required component invertible; the overlap isomorphism c handles the first component on V. Compare mapped biproducts with biproducts of images, then compose with the invertible counits.
